_why: What the built workbench is allowed to cost, in bytes, gzipped. `npm run check:weight` measures `dist/assets/**` plus `dist/index.html` after `npm run build` and fails when a metric is over its number or has nothing measured behind it. It also refuses a build older than its own sources (exit 2, naming the newer files, `--allow-stale` to override), because Run 165 quoted 950.3 kB measured from a `dist/` built before the features it was verifying. The budgets are hand-edited, deliberately: raise one with the reason in the commit, never by recording first. `entry_gzip` is what a first paint waits for — the document, its module script, the chunks it preloads and its stylesheets — and it is the number both splits moved: 627.5 kB in one chunk, 585.5 kB once the ten tabs became lazy chunks, **432.9 kB** once CodeMirror left the preload list too (the editor is a `React.lazy` boundary inside the runner, so the code, the Run button and the lesson text paint before the editor is parsed). Its budget came down to 470 kB for that reason: a static `@codemirror` import, or a tab folded back into the entry, fails here (Run 177 confirmed it: a statically imported Vim package pulled 149 kB of CodeMirror back into the entry's preloads, and the split into `vendor-vim` with a dynamic import put the entry back to 446 kB). `largest_js_gzip` was 614 kB when the app was one chunk and is 263 kB now, so its budget is 300 kB; the editor's own chunk (148.6 kB) is not the entry's problem any more but it still has to fit. `fonts` counts the woff2 files as they are (woff2 is already compressed, and every unicode-range subset is emitted — a Latin learner fetches roughly 140 kB of the 302 kB). `total` is a ceiling on the bundle as a whole, not the cost of a visit: the lazy chunks are all emitted whether or not a learner opens their tabs. `js_gzip` moved to 700 kB for the Vim keymap (`vendor-vim`, 39 kB): the chunk is fetched only when the keys are turned on — which is what keeps `entry_gzip` where it is — but this metric counts every emitted byte, so the ceiling has to know about it.
